current_content_summary: dlist d n (an [opaque] op) is the distribution of length-n lists sampled i.i.d. from d, built via `fold` over a dprod/dapply construction. Core lemmas: dlist0/dlist1/dlistS/dlistSr, dlist_add, dlist_djoin (relating dlist to DJoin.djoin over a fixed-length nseq), dlist1E/dlistE (mass function), supp_dlist(_size), dlist_ll/uni/fu, dlist_dmap, dlist_perm_eq, dlist_rev, dlist_dlist (nested dlist flattening), dlist_insert, dlist_setE/dlist_set2E (probability of a set of positions matching a predicate), and dmap_dlist_partial_perm (added r2026.03: reindexing a subset of positions via an injective function). Two abstract theories, `ParametricProgram` and `Program` (the latter fixing the distribution d as a theory parameter rather than a procedure argument), each define four equivalent module implementations of list-sampling -- Sample (one dlist draw), SampleCons (recursive head+tail draws), Loop (a while-loop building the list by prepending), LoopSnoc (a while-loop building the list by appending) -- with proved `equiv`s between all four. These are the standard lemmas used to justify rewriting a `for`-loop-based sampling routine as a single dlist draw or vice versa.
